newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI BAHT LOWER LATE, EYES IMF'S RESCUE PACKAGE.
newsitem.headline: THAI BAHT LOWER LATE, EYES IMF'S RESCUE PACKAGE.

text.p: The Thai baht was slightly lower in late Friday trade onshore with slow activities as the market awaited the conclusion of Monday's loan talks with the International Monetary Fund's (IMF), dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 31.25/31.35 to the dollar late compared with 31.10/31.20 in the morning.
"The baht was traded in very narrow range of around 31.20/31.30 today. There were not many transactions," one dealer at a European bank said.
The central bank on Friday said the weighted average interbank exchange rate was 31.517 per dollar against 31.618 on Thursday.

Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya will leave for Japan on Sunday to meet with the IMF and other institutions as well as about 10 potential donors including the United States and host Japan to secure loans to stabilise the troubled Thai economy.
Thailand is seeking $12-$15 billion in international loans to get its economy back on an even keel.
In offshore market, the baht was quoted at 30.73/30.83 late against 30.65/30.80 in early morning.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was at 12/15 satangs late in the domestic market and 18/28 in the offshore market.
